description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
Output: -20 participants are trained in a series of 4 weeks on the subject areas as described in the workplan
Achieved.
Over 20 participants were trained in a series of 3 weeks on the subject areas as described in the workplan. The last trainings week (week 4) was used to co-develop supportive materials for the incubation center and to train participants “on the job” in incubation support activities.
_-_ _Organisational development of business incubation centre ISPM_
Achieved.
This was the overall purpose of the training series. Through the various interventions CICIE-ISPM as an organisation has been strengthened. A need assessment was carried out to better understand the current situation, needs and interests. The incubation program has been revitalised, trainers are equipped and as Need assessment was carried out,
Other training focus areas that were achieved are:
- _Marketing, growth strategies and positioning._ This was identified as a key focus area to come to a product-market fit for incubates. Indicating the iterative process, whereby refining/redeveloping the innovation/business continuously based on market inputs is necessary. Time and tools to identify markets, carry out market assessments and to position yourself. Also how to develop a clear marketing strategy. All topics have been covered in the training series.
_-Business modelling and business finance_, the canvas business model together with the Lean start up methodology were applied with great positive feedback from the participants in using both methods. For the financial part we trained them on the Cashflow model as part of the Canvas model. Additionally Ivan Amade has taken them through a model of articles of association (legislative framework) to register an enterprise.
-_Product Development;_ in relation to this topic we focused on co-development of supportive materials for the incubation center to train participants “on the job” in incubation support activities.
_20 Participants apply lessons learnt in the training (as trainers of incubates) and in between training sessions in their work_
Yes see earlier reports on testimonies of applied lessons in their work.
_-_ _Backstopping from consultants for participants_
_Partnerships between relevant stakeholders and the Centre established_
10 project ideas developed by the participants that can be financeable. Partnerships on incubation between the participating Institutions in the training is also a positive outcome of the training series. As we trained participants from 4 Institutions. Instituto Superior Politécnico de Manica (ISPM) took the initiative to invite Instituto Superior Politécnico de Tete, Instituto Superior Politécnico de Songo, and Instituto Superior Politécnico de Gaza for this incubation training to boost female participation and general incubation support to students and graduates. Also connections between these institutions and Ivan Amade were established. As Ivan Amade has great connections with the government and banks (Banco Societe Generale Mozambique).

comment.narrative: 05-01-2023: Attention was given to making the training attractive to women, for example, by assessing the individual needs of the participants beforehand to be able to cater for them, by involving mainly female trainers, by checking for appropriate timing for the training in relation to gendered family responsibilities (considerate workshop times (finish early), and considerate in relation to school holidays), translation of the training as well as training materials and by ensuring appropriate gender sensitive language use.
